Help me refine this email with my state communications officer hat on and a good tone of voice. Subject: Transition plan: LSV Comms view and new incident categories (training from 5 October)

Hi all,

This season we're making two changes to how we work in State Communications: transitioning all officers to the LSV Comms view, and updating how we categorise incidents. We'll be running training ahead of these changes to make sure everyone is prepared. This email sets out the transition plan, including key dates and what's required of you. Please read it carefully and take note of the dates if you plan to continue taking shifts this season.

THE CHANGES IN BRIEF

We'll go through the detail of both changes in the training sessions, but here's a quick overview.

1. Moving to the LSV Comms view
We'll be asking all officers to use the LSV Comms view this season. Maintaining two interfaces means building and testing everything twice, and consolidating onto one lets us focus on making a single system work really well for you.

We're not switching the old dispatch interface off overnight. It will remain available during the transition, and we'll be following up with anyone still using it to understand why. That's about learning what isn't working for you in the new interface so we can fix it, not about catching anyone out. Our plan is to turn the old dispatch interface off by the end of the year.

2. Updating how we categorise incidents
We're updating our incident categories so they're more fit for purpose. This is foundational to how we grow as a service, and we'll explain the reasoning and the new categories in the sessions.

Both changes have been through extensive consultation with EMCaR, volunteer representatives and SLSQ, and we'd welcome your feedback throughout the training process.

THE TRANSITION PLAN

Training will run over six weeks in three two-week blocks, timed so we go live at the start of the season. We've chosen this window deliberately: it's early enough that we're not changing things mid-season when it's busy, but late enough that you'll be using the system regularly and can put your new skills into practice straight away, rather than learning them in the off season and forgetting before they're needed.

Block 1: Share the information (5 to 16 October)
What's changing, why, and what it means for you on shift, with time for questions. There are two sessions, each offered at two times. Please attend one time slot for each:
- Session 1: [Option A date/time] or [Option B date/time]
- Session 2: [Option A date/time] or [Option B date/time]

Block 2: Demo and trial (19 to 30 October)
A demonstration of the new functionality, with hands-on time in the training environment.
- [Session dates/times]

Block 3: Practice and Q&A (2 to 13 November)
Two weeks to experiment, review and digest in the training environment at your own pace, with Q&A sessions throughout.
- [Q&A dates/times]

Go live: Saturday 14 November (start of season)

Old dispatch interface turned off: by 31 December

THIS TRAINING IS REQUIRED

I want to be really clear on this one. This training is a key competency for your role. If you haven't completed it by 14 November, you won't be able to be rostered on for shifts until it's done.

If you can't make any of the sessions, please contact Dave as early as possible and he'll work with you on alternate arrangements.

WANT TO HELP SHAPE THE DESIGN?

We're finalising the user experience designs now, and we'd love some of you to be involved. Development starts this week, so designs need to be finalised by Friday 9 October. We're planning an initial session early next week, and it will need some short-notice availability between now and 9 October. If you're keen, let Dave or Flynn know as soon as possible.

WHERE TO GET MORE INFORMATION

- The training sessions are the main place to learn about the changes and ask questions
- User guides will be provided ahead of go live
- Dave for session bookings and alternate arrangements
- Dave or Flynn for the UX design sessions
- Me, anytime, if you'd like to talk any of i
